title: WHO ICD-11 Reference Guide - Part 1: Traditional Medicine Module 2
publication_info: WHO ICD-11 Reference Guide (Section 1.5 Traditional Medicine)
text: The Traditional Medicine chapter enables standardized recording of traditional medicine conditions and patterns, including Ayurveda, Siddha, and Unani morbidity concepts, designed to be used optionally alongside standard biomedical classifications in ICD-11.

title: National AYUSH Morbidity and Standardized Terminologies Electronic (NAMASTE) Portal
source: Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India
text: National Ayurveda Morbidity Codes (NAMC) define diagnostic conditions, dosha derangements, and clinical manifestations based on classical Ayurvedic compendia (Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita).

title: Charaka Samhita - Chikitsa Sthana (Chapter 3: Jwara Chikitsitam)
source: National Institute of Indian Medical Heritage (NIIMH), CCRAS
text: Jwara is characterized by Santapa (elevated heat/temperature), Aruchi (anorexia), Trishna (excessive thirst), Angamarda (body ache), and Hridvyatha (restlessness).

title: ICD-11 Entity Specification: MG26 Symptoms or signs involving the body temperature
text: MG26 covers pyrexia of unknown origin, hyperpyrexia, and elevated body temperature in response to systemic inflammation, infection, or thermoregulatory disturbance.

title: ICD-11 Entity Specification: MD30 Cough
text: MD30 describes cough as a sudden, repetitive reflex response to airway irritation or respiratory conditions, corresponding closely with Ayurvedic Kasa roga.

title: WHO Fact Sheet: Seasonal Influenza - Clinical Features and Supportive Care
text: Treatment should aim to relieve symptoms. People with the flu should rest and drink plenty of liquids. Most people will recover on their own within a week. Medical care may be needed in severe cases and for people with risk factors.

title: WHO Integrated Management of Adolescent and Adult Illness (IMAI) District Clinician Manual
publication_info: ISBN: 9789241548281 (Hospital Care for Adolescents and Adults)
passage_location: Chapter 1: Clinical Triage and Emergency Assessment of Febrile Illness
text: Emergency triage assessment identifies general danger signs requiring immediate physician intervention: altered level of consciousness, central cyanosis, respiratory distress, severe prostration, or persistent high fever with stiff neck or petechial rash.

title: NHS Health A to Z: Cough Self-Care and Home Management
publication_info: NHS Health A to Z (Reviewed April 2025)
passage_location: Section: How you can treat a cough yourself
text: There's usually no need to see a GP if you have a cough. You should: rest, drink plenty of fluids, try to stay at home and avoid contact with other people if you have a high temperature or you do not feel well enough to do your normal activities.

title: NHS Clinical Guidelines: Acute Cough Warning Signs & Urgent Referral Criteria
publication_info: NHS Health A to Z (Reviewed April 2025)
passage_location: Section: Urgent advice & When to see a GP
text: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if: your cough is very bad or quickly gets worse – for example, you have a hacking cough or cannot stop coughing, you feel very unwell, you have chest pain, you find it hard to breathe, you're coughing up blood. See a GP if: you've had a cough for more than 3 weeks (persistent cough).

title: WHO Paediatric Emergency Triage, Assessment and Treatment: Care of Critically-Ill Children
passage_location: Section: Emergency Triage Assessment - Airway and Breathing
text: Priority emergency signs include central cyanosis, severe respiratory distress, marked chest indrawing, or inability to complete full sentences, which require immediate oxygen therapy and clinical resuscitation.

title: WHO Fact Sheet: Musculoskeletal Conditions
text: Musculoskeletal conditions significantly limit mobility and dexterity. Management focuses on maintaining physical capacity, functional mobility, gentle range-of-motion activity, and early primary health service delivery to prevent long-term functional impairment.
